destinations.name: Cubic
destinations.mapBlurb: One player walks the outside of a cube, the other is trapped inside. Neither can see the other's screen.
destinations.mapBlurbPhone: One player outside a cube, one trapped inside.
destinations.description: A two-player co-op puzzle game in the browser. One player walks the outside of a cube, the other is trapped inside, and neither can see the other's screen. You solve all six faces by talking through the walls.
destinations.heroAlt: Cubic world: the game's pixel-art cube with its biome faces
destinations.problem: Keeping both players oriented as they walk across cube edges. Every face has its own "up," and the inside view is a mirror of the outside, so one shared cube-math library runs on both the client and the server to keep them in agreement.

shots.alt: Cubic outside view: a bright pixel-art biome on the cube's surface

shots.caption: INSIDE PLAYER
shots.alt: Cubic inside view: a dark lantern-lit room inside the cube

destinations.name: Lens
destinations.chipNote: Switch to VALIDATED SCORING only once the full labelled set (407 answers) has been run. Until then use EVIDENCE-CHECKED SCORES.
destinations.mapBlurb: Interview prep that scores every answer on four dimensions and highlights the exact phrases behind each score.
destinations.mapBlurbPhone: Interview prep that scores answers and shows the phrases behind each score.
destinations.description: Paste a job posting and Lens writes five interview questions for that role. Answer by typing or by voice, and it scores you on four dimensions, highlighting the exact phrase behind every score.
destinations.heroAlt: A real Lens answer with highlighted phrases, under a moving magnifying glass
destinations.problem: Making the score something you can check, not just an AI saying "good answer." Every score has to quote your answer, and the server rejects any quote that is not really in your text. Voice mode broke that at first, because speech-to-text splits on every pause, so I wrote a transcript builder that only ends a sentence on a real pause.

shots.caption: HIGHLIGHTED ANSWER
shots.alt: A Lens answer with the phrases behind each score highlighted

shots.caption: FOUR SCORES
shots.alt: Lens score breakdown: completeness, substance density, reasoning, correctness

destinations.world: assets/lens-real.webp with the gliding gold loupe (see design/Main.html, .loupe2 keyframes)

otherProjects.name: Turtle Trips AI
otherProjects.description: Tell it where you want to go and when, and it plans a multi-day trip with a photo for every stop and a route on the map for each day.
otherProjects.heroAlt: Turtle Trips itinerary: day plan with photos next to a route map of Vancouver
otherProjects.problem: Gemini answers in loose text, but a trip planner needs days, times, and real places. I had it return JSON, turned that into page templates, pulled photos from Google Places, and sent each day's stops to the Directions API to draw the route.

otherProjects.name: Amenity Recommender
otherProjects.description: Type what you like, such as coffee or sushi, and it maps the closest Vancouver places that match. It can also read the GPS data in your photos and show what you walked past.
otherProjects.heroAlt: Map of downtown Vancouver with a photo walk and nearby places
otherProjects.problem: Matching what people type to OpenStreetMap tags. Plain text matching missed obvious hits, like "sushi" against a place tagged as a Japanese restaurant, so we compared sentence embeddings instead, then kept only places within the distance you set.

otherProjects.name: Pipeline Simulator
otherProjects.description: A cycle-by-cycle simulator of a 2-wide, 5-stage processor pipeline, written in C++. It replays real instruction traces of hundreds of megabytes and measures how pipeline depth changes run time.
otherProjects.heroAlt: A 2-wide, 5-stage processor pipeline with instructions moving through it
otherProjects.problem: Getting the hazards right at speed. The simulator tracks data, control and structural hazards every cycle, and the traces were too big to scan from the start each run. I added a sparse index that remembers a file offset every 100,000 lines, so each of the 72 runs jumps straight to its starting instruction.

shots.caption: RESULTS, 72 RUNS
shots.alt: Bar chart: average run time drops as pipeline depth goes from 1 to 4 on all three traces

shots.caption: SIMULATOR CORE
shots.alt: C++ code for the pipeline stages, hazard flags and sparse trace index

otherProjects.world: animated SVG pipeline, 5 stages x 2 lanes with stepping tokens (see design/Main.html and design/DetailPipeline.html)

otherProjects.name: NutriFit
otherProjects.description: A meal planning web app for people with fitness goals. Find recipes that fit your diet and allergies, save meals, find grocery stores nearby, and ask the community.

otherProjects.problem: The Recipe Finder, on the Edamam API, with diet and allergy filters and search by several ingredients at once. I also added a store finder that maps grocery stores near your postal code, and wrote the tests for sign up, login, recipes, and the community board.

experience.summary: Built nearly all of the web app for a settlement platform with 500+ users, on a production database shared with the mobile app.
bullets: Shipped an AI assistant with retrieval over a vector knowledge base, plus AI resume and cover letter tools, with per-user quotas and provider fallback
Built a scheduled pipeline pulling events from 12 sources; traced 30 of 69 mislabelled events to a field the sources never set, and fixed it
Fixed a race where out-of-order saves wiped user edits, by serializing writes through one promise chain
Shipped the app in 7 languages, including right-to-left Arabic, across 120+ reviewed pull requests
